evidence.Act Name/Web name/Doc name: Gujarat Town Planning and Urban Development Act, 1976 (President's Act No. 27 of 1976), consolidated text with amendments up to Act 2 of 1999, hosted on the Rajkot Urban Development Authority (RUDA) website
evidence.Chapter: Whole Act checked (Chapters I–VIII). The only 'Board' in the Act is the Board of Appeal under the Town Planning Scheme provisions (Sections 54–60).
evidence.Provision: No section sets up a state-level town and country planning board or spatial planning board. Section 55 (Constitution of Board of Appeal) is the only provision that creates a 'Board'.
evidence.Page Number: No page applies, because no such provision exists. Section 55 is on p. 43–44 of the PDF.

quote: The State Government shall, from time to time by an order published in the Official Gazette, constitute a Board of Appeal for hearing and deciding appeals under Section 54.
comments: Gujarat's town and country planning law is the Gujarat Town Planning and Urban Development Act, 1976 (GTPUDA). I read the full text of the consolidated version on RUDA's site, which a person can open, and went through every section heading, Sections 1 to 124. The Act sets up these bodies: area development authorities (Sections 5–6/6A), urban development authorities (Section 22), a Planning Committee inside a local authority that is designated as an area development authority (Section 6), Town Planning Officers (Section 50) and a Board of Appeal (Section 55). The Act also names the 'Chief Town Planner' in Section 2(vii), but only as a government officer. I searched the text for 'Board', 'Council', 'Committee', 'advise' and 'policy'. None of these turned up a state-level planning board, council or other body charged with state planning policy or reform, whether under a 'shall' clause or a 'may' clause. The Board of Appeal is a quasi-judicial body led by a District Judge-level President. It hears appeals against Town Planning Officer decisions and has no policy mandate. Because the Act has no enabling provision, there is no notification to look for under the 'may' route. I also searched the web for a state town planning board or spatial planning board in Gujarat and found nothing. Bodies such as GUDC (Gujarat Urban Development Company), GIDB (Gujarat Infrastructure Development Board) and the Town Planning & Valuation Department are not statutory planning boards with this mandate. So Part A = NO, and Part B = NO because it only counts if Part A is YES. Things a reviewer should check: (1) The consolidated text records amendments only up to Act 2 of 1999. Later amendments, such as those in the 2010s, should be checked, although I found no sign that any of them added a state planning board. (2) Two other copies of the Act could not be used as the citation: the official India Code PDF timed out during the link check, and the Town Planning Department's acts page returned a 404 error. A person may want to swap in an official Government of Gujarat copy if one can be reached.
